rationale: ONTOLOGY `overrides`, and the SYMBOL loss underneath it. A pure virtual is how C++ spells an interface — there is no `interface` keyword and no `implements` clause, so `= 0` IS the construct, and it was invisible twice over. (1) `virtual bool ReportContext(const Context&) = 0;` parses as `declaration > init_declarator > function_declarator`, and `init_declarator` was missing from the declarator-wrapper list in `getFunctionDetails`, which returned null; the caller takes the function's SYMBOL and its SCOPE out of that result, so the interface's own methods were published NOWHERE. Measured on `cpp-sample/include/benchmark/reporter.h`: `BenchmarkReporter` published `ReportRunsConfig`, `Finalize`, `List` and nine more, and NOT `ReportContext` or `ReportRuns` — and with the base's members absent from the virtual registry, `overrides` fired ZERO times over 128 admitted files carrying 77 written `override` specifiers in 26 of them. (2) The override matcher built its parameter signature with a SECOND, weaker declared-name lookup (a `declarator`-FIELD chain only), so a parameter declared `const Context& context` — whose name sits under a `reference_declarator` as a plain NAMED child — resolved to no name and the whole text, NAME INCLUDED, became the 'type'. Two declarations of the same type with different parameter names then hashed differently. A name is not part of a C++ signature, so those are one signature. The rule is now the analyzer's single declared-name funnel, the same one the published `parameters` payload uses; the two had drifted into a second answer about a second question and the divergence was invisible because the payload's own fixture passed. `Hidden` is the control in the other direction: a genuinely different parameter TYPE must still NOT produce an edge, because C++ name hiding is not virtual dispatch — a type-only signature that ignored types would pass every case above and be wrong about all of them.

expectSymbols.note: THE `init_declarator` CASE. `Decorated` is macro-decorated, and a pure virtual inside a macro-decorated class parses as `declaration > init_declarator > function_declarator` rather than `field_declaration > function_declarator` — so a shallow declarator lookup missed it and `getFunctionDetails` returned null, taking the method's SYMBOL and its SCOPE with it. Measured over the two pinned corpora: 7 pure-virtual sites, 4 in the direct shape (published) and 3 in the `init_declarator` shape (published NOWHERE) — `benchmark/reporter.h:132`, `:136` and `benchmark_api.h:146`, which are `BenchmarkReporter.ReportContext`, `BenchmarkReporter.ReportRuns` and `Benchmark.Run`.

expectSymbols.name: Impl
expectSymbols.note: THE ROW THAT FAILS PRE-FIX, and it took a second row to find. `class IFACE_EXPORT Impl : public IFACE_EXPORT Decorated {` is the A2 shape, so the pre-fix reader published this class as `Decorated` — which meant the `tick`/`flush` symbols it then owned still carried `ownerName: Decorated` and the obvious symbol assertion PASSED for the wrong reason. Pinning the line is what makes the assertion about the declaration rather than about a name that happens to exist: pre-fix there is no symbol named `Impl` at all, and `Impl`'s members were attributed to its own base.

It is here so a future 'fix' that over-matches is caught by the same fixture. STALE-PIN FIX 2026-10-17: this row pinned `signature-match` (0.9, the inference arm), but the fixture's own `Same::ReportContext` is written `override` — so under M14-HONESTY-CONTRACT §4 the edge is a 1.0 FACT and its code is `override-keyword+signature-match`, exactly as cpp/reason-code-4 pins the same shape. The strength of the assertion is unchanged (same-spelling control); only the evidence class it is asserted at was corrected, upward.

(2) THE CASE. `const std::vector<Run>& report` in the base and `const std::vector<Run>& reports` in the derived are the SAME C++ signature — names are not part of it. Pre-fix this produced no edge at all, and the pre-fix `reporter.h` count was 2 of 4 with both survivors being the zero-argument methods, which is exactly the population where 'no parameters' accidentally agrees with 'parameters whose names happen to match'.

the macro-decorated base clause: the grammar puts `Name : access` in an ERROR node, so `base_class_clause` is never produced and this edge did not exist. Without it there is no `classBases` entry, and a `classBases` entry is the precondition for ANY override on this pair.

Every class-scope method registers in the virtual registry by design (C++ virtual dispatch does not require the keyword), so the guard here is the SIGNATURE — and `Hidden`'s rows above show the signature still discriminates. A matcher that resolved by name alone would emit this row and both rows above.
